sentences.text: This criminal miscellaneous case is filed to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.1/2017 on the file of the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Palakkad.
It is a private complaint filed by the 2nd respondent against the petitioners and another on behalf of the husband of the 2 nd respondent Sri.Haridasan.
The offences alleged in the complaint are under Sections 405, 406, 409, 120B, 418, 420, 464 and 465 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
Annexure-A is the complaint.

The complaint was filed by the 2nd respondent alleging that the Fixed Deposit receipts in the name of the 2 nd respondent and her family share certificates in the name of Haridasan as well as blank cheques and blank signed papers obtained from Haridasan 2024:KER:75289 CRL.MC NO. 2651 OF 2017 by the accused persons and by manipulation, the funds to the tune of Rs.1 crores covered by those documents were were got credited to the account of the HDFC Limited.
It is submitted that all the Fixed Deposits were made by Haridasan in the joint name of himself and wife, and himself and her daughter.
Hence it is alleged that the accused committed the offence.

According to the petitioners,
even if the entire allegations are accepted, no offence is made out.
Hence this criminal miscellaneous case.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor.
I also heard the learned counsel for the 2nd respondent.
3. The counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are senior officers of Housing Development Finance Corporation (HDFC) Ltd working at Mumbai and Coimbatore.
The 1st petitioner is the Vice Chairman and C.E.O of HDFC having his office in Mumbai.
Petitioners 2 to 2024:KER:75289 CRL.MC NO. 2651 OF 2017 are the Manager, Senior Officer and Regional Manager of HDFC at the regional office, HDFC House, Coimbatore.

According to the petitioners, the husband of the 2 nd respondent was Resident Manager in charge of the Palakkad branch of HDFC since 2003 until he was dismissed from service on 25.02.2010, for his proved criminal misconduct and criminal breach of trust in the matter of defrauding HDFC and misappropriation of the funds of HDFC to the tune of more than Rs.9 crores while he was working in Palakkad branch of HDFC.

According to the petitioners, Haridasan was a hardworking and well behaved person, and therefore,
all the loans processed and sanctioned by him as Manager of the branch were approved as such in the regional office or other higher offices of the HDFC.

As resident manager of Palakkad branch of HDFC Ltd, Haridasan was responsible for accepting, processing and appraisal of all loans, collection of legal documents for arranging disbursements, 2024:KER:75289 CRL.MC NO. 2651 OF 2017 maintenance of property documents, coordinating the work of Direct Service Associates (DSA) of the Company and monitoring their activities and programmes.
The DSAs were recommended by Haridasan for marketing of housing loans.
It is submitted that the customers used to approach the branch mainly through the DSAs and directly to the branch only occasionally.

It is submitted that the Resident Manager Haridasan, after processing the loan application and scrutiny of documents,
upload the same in the Computer system.
It is also submitted that he used to create files in his I.D.
The original files relating to the loans are shown to be scrutinized and satisfied by Haridasan before his recommendation.
The details of the customers are also uploaded in the system.

It is submitted that on the basis of the facts and details available in the system as uploaded by Haridasan,
Coimbatore office used to approve the recommendation of the Manager Haridasan who was empowered to recommend loans up to Rs.30 Lakhs.

sentences.text: The officers of the Coimbatore office, who have been reposing absolute trust on Sri. Haridasan used to approve all his recommendation till December 2009 is the submission.

But discreet enquires made by petitioners 2 to 4 and certain other officers of the HDFC, on coming to know about certain discrepancies in the loan transaction of Palakkad branch revealed that the Manager, Haridasan on his own and in conspiracy with D.S. Agents and some others defrauded the bank.
Bogus and forged documents were submitted and uploaded in the computer and huge amount is disbursed.
Accordingly, HDFC obtained explanation from Mr.Haridasan.

It is further submitted that Mr.Haridasan admitted his guilt in relation to the acts of fraud detected by petitioners 2 to 4 and other Senior officers and gave it in writing by his letter dated 30-12- 2009 addressed to the Company viz HDFC Ltd.

Annexure B is the letter written in his own handwriting confessing various types of manipulation, forgeries and cheating done 2024:KER:75289 CRL.MC NO. 2651 OF 2017 by him in the matter of 88 loans recommended by him as the resident manager of Palakkad Branch.
It is submitted that Mr. Haridasan had assured that he will recoup the entire amount, which was misappropriated by him.

Pursuant to that, nine cumulative deposits of Haridasan and his wife T.K.
Geetha, who is the 2nd respondent herein, with the HDFC were discharged by them by signing the deposit receipts and produced before the office of the HDFC at Coimbatore with a covering letter,
requesting to adjust the proceeds of the said deposits against the housing loan accounts created by Mr.Haridasan.
Annexure-C is the covering letter dated 30.12.2009 written by Haridasan and addressed to the Branch Manager HDFC Ltd, Coimbatore.

It is also submitted that four other fixed deposits made in the name of his minor daughter Arunitha with Haridasan as the guardian and joint holder also were discharged for encashment before the Coimbatore branch of the HDFC.

The same were encashed and the proceedings of the four 2024:KER:75289 CRL.MC NO. 2651 OF 2017 fixed deposits was credited to the SB account of the daughter with Gwalior branch of HDFC, where also Haridasan was the guardian.
After the said credit, Haridasan issued cheque for the said credited amount in favour of the HDFC Coimbatore Branch and Annexure-D is the covering letter, is the submission.

Total amount covered by the said 13 deposits were Rs.13,67,238/-.
5.
It is also submitted that all the deposits were made during the period 2006 to 2008, during which Haridasan was the Resident Manager of Palakkad Branch.
It is further submitted that, the amount thus credited/paid is below 13% of the amount defrauded and dishonestly and wrongfully gained by Haridasan and his accomplices.

It is also submitted that Mr.Haridasan transferred his 13215 number of HDFC shares to the account of the HDFC, after complying with all formalities and proceedings and submitting necessary applications before the Company Secretary and IL & FS investments, Mumbai.
He transferred 2024:KER:75289 CRL.MC NO. 2651 OF 2017 an amount of Rs.38.44 lakhs rupees from his account to the account of HDFC.

From the very same account,
Mr.Haridasan transferred another amount of Rs.47.40 lakhs also to the account of HDFC, is the submission.
Further on 26.12.2009, Mr.Haridasan transferred an amount of Rs.56.15 lakhs from his account.

6. Considering the magnitude of the fraudulent and dishonest acts of Haridasan and the huge loss sustained by HDFC due to the said acts, Haridasan was dismissed from service as per proceedings of Senior General Manager, Sri.Mathew Joseph, Regional Office, HDFC, Chennai.

sentences.text:
As there was no further response from Haridasan, HDFC filed criminal complaint against Haridasan and on the basis of the said complaint, Crime No. 549 of 2010 was registered at Palakkad Town South Police station on 5-8-2010 against Haridasan and four others for the offences punishable under Section 409,
2024:KER:75289 CRL.MC NO. 2651 OF 2017 465, 471, 477A and 120B IPC is the submission.

The accusation in the FIR is that accused Nos. 1 to 5 pursuant to a criminal conspiracy hatched by them,
defrauded HDFC to the tune of more than Rs. 9 Crores (Rs. 9,0000000) on the basis of fictitious loan applications and forged and fabricated documents.

Subsequently, several other cases were got registered at Palakkad Town South Police Station against Haridasan and his accomplices as Crime No. 496/2012, Crime No. 497/2012, Crime No. 520 of 2012, Crime No. 809/2012, Crime No.
1292/2012, Crime No. 327/2013, Crime No. 328/2013, Crime No. 329/2013, Crime No. 823/2013 etc is the submission.
7. The investigation in all those cases were handed over to the CBCID.
Investigation is completed and charge sheets are filed in few of the cases is the further submission.
It is submitted that Mr.Haridasan absconded when Crime No.549 of 2010 of Palakkad Town South Police station was registered.

Suppressing the above facts, the 2 nd 2024:KER:75289 CRL.MC NO. 2651 OF 2017 respondent who is a total stranger to the HDFC, except that she happened to be the wife of Haridasan filed Annexure A complaint, exactly two years after HDFC detected the fraudulent acts committed by Haridasan and Haridasan made a confession, as per his Annexure-B letter and the part of the amount defrauded and misappropriated by Haridasan was credited by Haridasan to the account of HDFC Ltd Coimbatore Branch
is the submission.
Annexure- A complaint was filed on 23-12-2011.
But the sworn statement of the complainant, who is the 2 nd respondent herein was recorded on 19-9-2012.
Anneuxre-A1 is the sworn statement of the 2nd respondent.
Even after recording the sworn statement of the 2nd respondent, the Court below could not take cognizance as the complainant had no direct knowledge about the allegations.
Thereafter, Mr.Haridasan was arrested by the investigating officers of CBCID in 2012 and he was later on released on bail by the Court.

At last, after a long lapse of 5 years, Haridasan was 2024:KER:75289 CRL.MC NO. 2651 OF 2017 brought before Court by the 2 nd respondent on 1-11-2016 and on that day, he gave a statement before the court, which appears to be the defense proposed to be taken by him, in the prosecution proceedings pending against him is the further submission.
Annexure-F is the statement of Haridasan recorded by the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Palakkad.
Based on the same, the learned Magistrate took cognizance and issued summons to the petitioners.
According to the petitioners, even if the entire allegations are accepted, no offence is made out.
8. A perusal of Annexure-A complaint does not disclose the year, month or date of the alleged commission of the offence.
It also does not disclose the place of occurrence.
The source of information is only hearsay in complaint.
As I observed earlier, after filing Annexure-A, the sworn statement of Mr.Haridasan was recorded after 5 years.
Till then, there was no complaint at all against any of the petitioners.

On 01.11.2016, for the first time, 2024:KER:75289 CRL.MC NO. 2651 OF 2017 Haridasan came out with a story that on 15.12.2009, he was threatened, assaulted and induced to write a confession letter and to hand over fixed deposit receipts, share certificates, blank signed cheques and blank signed papers etc. at Coimbatore office of the HDFC Bank and the amount covered by the FD receipts and share certificates were credited to the account of HDFC at its own K.M.Mistry vs State on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46244207/
5 Coimbatore branch.

sentences.text: As per his statement, all the transactions relating to the offence occurred in Coimbatore and the alleged offences were committed in the office of the 4th petitioner at Coimbatore and the amounts were credited to the account of HDFC at Coimbatore branch.
No part of the transaction occurred in the Kerala State.

This is clear from the sworn statement given by Mr.
Haridasan, even though the same is not mentioned in the complaint.
This aspect is not considered by the learned Magistrate, while taking cognizance.

Moreover, from a reading of the complaint along with the sworn statement of the 2 nd 2024:KER:75289 CRL.MC NO. 2651 OF 2017 respondent and Mr.Haridasan, it is clear that it is a case set up by Mr.Haridasan as a defense in the cases registered against him at the instance of HDFC.
I am of the considered opinion that, in the facts and circumstances of this case, the continuation of the prosecution against the petitioners are not necessary.
But, I make it clear that quashing the proceedings will not stand in the way of the husband of the 2nd respondent in taking appropriate defense in his case, in accordance with law.
But, the proceedings against the petitioners can be quashed.
Therefore, this criminal miscellaneous case is allowed.
All further proceedings against the petitioners in C.C.No. 1/2017 on the file of the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Palakkad are quashed.
